text_fidelity_a:
Neewer TT560 Flash Speedlite for Canon Nikon Panasonic Olympus Pentax and Other DSLR Cameras，Digital Cameras with Standard Hot Shoe Failed to flash about every 25th go. When it did flash, output was inconsistent - often a half a stop darker.

I purchased this just to use as a slave to be triggered by another flash - a Yongnuo 560-II. I figured this one looked pretty similar and cost a lot less (though it's less powerful and doesn't have zooming or an LCD screen, doesn't go into sleep mode. I didn't need those things). The Yongnuo was about $60 and this one was $37 at the time.

I would should 100 shots of the same setup with the same 2 flashes -- everything the same (this was for macro - close up work). Over and over again I'd find dark frames on the Neewer TT560 side and the Yongnuo was dead on every time.

If you're shooting your nephew's 5th Birthday Party and don't care if the shots come out (why aren't you using a phone cam?), then this is OK. If you care at all, pay the $25 extra and get the Yongnuo. (Actually, Yongnuo has a 460-ii model for about $40. I haven't tried that, but I'd give it a shot before this one).
text_fidelity_b: Neewer TT560 Flash Speedlite for Canon Nikon Panasonic Olympus Pentax and Other DSLR Cameras，Digital Cameras with Standard Hot Shoe

text_fidelity_a:
Stanley 33959 ShopMax Power Hub 20-Feet 4-Outlet Cord Reel , Yellow Why is the cable size and breaker on this thing so undersized when it is presumably (due to the fact that it is Stanley Max) for running power tools? 16AWG and 13A is actually a bottleneck compared to a standard 15A 14AWG household circuit. Worse is that it is a huge bottleneck compared to the 12AWG 20A circuits I put in work and kitchen areas to accommodate the many tools (e.g., miter saws, medium sized air compressors, etc.) and appliances (e.g., microwaves) that push the envelope on the 15A circuits.

Point is, right off the bat, I can't run large tools on this thing (and that includes some plug-in-lawn equipment), and I can't run most medium sized tools two at a time on this thing (good drills, planers, grinders, etc. often draw around 9A), so what's the point of the multiple outlets except, granted, that you don't have to unplug one to plug the other in over and over again if working with two tools alternately.

On the flip side, this lighter gauge cable does allow this power hub to be lighter and easier to deal with. It does roll up nicely and I like that the cord can be attached on the side so it doesn't unravel itself.

But I think the outlets should be spaced a little further a part, given that the size could accommodate that. That would allow larger plugs, and maybe even some AC adapters to fit. I also think 20 ft. is way too short, especially for the reel setup (it's not that hard to untangle 20ft.) and the fact that this thing is probably large enough to hold more.

You could use it for Christmas lights or something like that - except it is not a true weatherproof cord - or some low power hobby in the house. This has no quality issues, and there are plenty of uses for it, but the name has me thinking it is trying to be in the tool market. To be really effective in that market, it should be 12AWG, accept 20A plugs, be minimum 50' long, and have the outlets spaced slightly further apart.
text_fidelity_b: Stanley 33959 ShopMax Power Hub 20-Feet 4-Outlet Cord Reel , Yellow

Take time to position because while the tape adheres well it looses its stickiness after being removed and repositioned. The infrared remote must be in line of sight for it to work. The way around that is to use the app. The app works with both android and iOS. The app has a voice control which I found to be inconsistent and a private listening feature that lets you use your phone headphones and mute the TV.

Performance is mixed. navigating and launching is slow. Netflix in particular really dragged. but playing content was excellent with no lag or problems. the channel selection is good with pretty much everything you would want available.

This is not bad for a budget streamer. there are definitely downsides, the ir remote, the lack of speed, the need for a cable. but it does work and is small enough for travel. I am frequently on the road for business and this does expand the limited options of hotel televisions. If you are on a budget and don't need or want the features that are available on pricier models this low end streamer will get the job done.

The USB ports are tucked right in between the cord wrap spot and the place to plug in larger plugs, so if one isn't blocking your USB ports, the other is.

In addition, I kind of wish that the majority of the plugs were spaced farther apart. I have a few electronics that have very small boxy plugs, and those don't fit right next to one another on the main area of the plug strip. The only thing that will fit on those plugs without overlapping are the traditional small plugs that are on lamps and other uncomplicated items. I don't have too many of those, and I'm guessing that most people buy plug strips because they have a bunch of electronics, almost all of which would have those bigger boxy plugs.

That said, the surge protector feature is absolutely effective, and I know this because we had PG&E replacing some poles in our neighborhood recently and we had many incidences of brownouts, surges, and spotty power, and this unit kept any harm from coming to any of my electronics that were plugged into it.

And while it is easy to make design suggestions, I have to say that I haven't found the perfect plug strip yet. Almost all of them seem to have some design characteristics that make them not quite ideal. While this unit is not perfectly designed with regards to the placement of the USB ports and the spacing of the regular plugs, it is certainly a high-quality, very functional unit that does what it says it does, and I trust the Belkin brand that it's going to function for some time. This plug strip is also nice in that it has a space so that you can mount it on the wall or on the back of your desk if you so desire.

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras I've always wanted a Canon macro flash but the cost was just too much for something that I would not use very regularly. This macro light, while not a flash, is a very affordable alternative that works very well.

It is a 48 LED light. There's no communication with the camera - it's not a flash, nor can it be controlled in any way by the camera itself. The controls are manual, and allow you to use all the LEDs, half of them (left) or half of them (right). It is powered by 2 AA batteries or by an AC adapter (included). The battery pack mounts on the hotshoe, and the macro light is affixed to the lens barrel.

The battery pack fit fine on my Canon 5D Mark II, but the manufacturer includes a note with the device that says an additional adapter will be needed for it to fit the hotshoe of Sony, Konica and Minolta DSLR cameras.

It comes with two diffusers (white and orange) that are easy to put on and take off. It also comes with six lens thread adapter rings for all the usual sizes - 49mm, 52, 55, 58, 62, and 67. You attach the adapter ring to front of lens, and slot the light over the ring.

No problems fitting it to a Canon L 100mm macro lens. Fit well and was secure during use.

It throws a good amount of light on a ultra close-range subject, which may be otherwise shaded by the close proximity of your lens, or for other reasons be hard to light properly. But, there are limitations - don't expect this to throw a lot of light like a light panel would on a subject at medium distance.

The build quality is better than expected given the price. It's all plastic, but seems more than durable enough for home use.

I'm very pleased with this. It's a small fraction of the cost of a Canon ring light and, while it does not have flash capabilities, it remains a very helpful addition to lighting those tricky macro shots. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras 48 LED unit - (since several items are listed under one product ID)
Positives:
- It is what it looks like, does what it claims to do, and basically works
- cheap
- comes with an AC adapter!! Wow. You can pay a lot for a light that doesn't

Negatives: I'm using this for Macro work (I'm new to macro) so that's the perspective I'm coming from
- Not Bright Enough! It's just not all that bright. Not enough to light a subject by itself for macro purposes. I doubt it's adequate for more than a highlight for portraiture. This is why 2 stars. If a light doesn't light - it's not a light.

Really that's it. This is not a knock to the light (and not why I gave it a low rating), but if you are planning on using it for macro, buy a flash instead. A flash will not only have higher output, but will help freeze the camera shake (a big macro problem). Also, I thought the full time light would be better for live insects (you can see what you're doing!), but it's the opposite. You need the flash to freeze action. Not a criticism (this light does not advertise itself as a flash), but something to know.

UPDATE: I used it a couple more times. I am finding it more useful than initially when very close in. I would still strongly recommend a flash for this unless you have a compelling reason for continuous illumination (e.g you're waiting for a bug to crawl into frame and it's too dark to see otherwise. Though the lights would probably scare the bug). If you have a pretty solid tripod setup, this can work for longer exposure macro. Not great though. Upped to 3 stars.

Kingston 8 GB Class 4 SDHC Flash Memory Card SD4/8GB I ordered this part for use with a new Audibon Birdcam. The Kingston memory card failed in just over a month. It was unreadable by several PCs and a Mac. Amazon said to contact Kingston directly (Kingston memories carry a lifetime warranty). Kingston had me return the memory (my expense) and issued an RMA. They used "UPS Mail Innovations" to ship.
UPS MI is an el-cheapo service that uses the USPS mid-stream and for final delivery. Predictably, the shipment to me was lost by the USPS and tracking information abruptly stopped. It took four telephone calls to Kingston, the final call being to a supervisor, to get another parts shipped. The CS reps kept reading me the dead tracking info in which the shipment was "out for delivery" in another state and past due by several days. It's been three weeks since I sent the part back. I'm waiting for the second RMA part to arrive.
I'm not sure that Sandisk memories are fundamentally any better, but I can say that I never suffered a failure of any of their many memories I own.

text_fidelity_a:
Legrand - Wiremold Cable Management Kit, Cord Organizer and Hider, Concealer, C210S Cord Cover Kit, White I'm sure they do it for shipping purposes and to appeal to homeowners without tools, but I don't like that they give you multiple short pieces instead of fewer long pieces that you could cut down to appropriate size. That just means you need more couplers; each additional coupler decreases the appeal of the final installation.

Honestly, I hate surface mounted conduit. But there are times when it is required, and in those cases better than nothing. I own my home, so of course I put all permanent links properly inside the walls, but even then, there are times when the Cat/RG/other jacks are not directly behind the furniture holding the devices that need the cables. In these cases, I prefer to mount these with screws, and then caulk and paint them into the painted baseboards so they blend in better, although they have made these with tape for truly temporary installations.

There is just one connector for an inside corner and an outside corner (on the x/z axis). And in my opinion, these are the only two you should really need, and you probably need more of them. I am never going vertical up walls with cables; I just go from the jack along the baseboard to behind the furniture...if I need more than that, I'm afraid I need to just stop being lazy and tear down a wall or something.

I get that if you are in an apartment or a rental property, you may need more flexibility with this. But in my opinion, if you can't do a proper wall-mount TV install without surface-mount conduit, then you should just use a TV stand as God intended because this is not enough to make cables acceptable in such an install (although honestly, it is better than nothing).
text_fidelity_b: Legrand - Wiremold Cable Management Kit, Cord Organizer and Hider, Concealer, C210S Cord Cover Kit, White

They're comfortable, simple and elegant design, and with good sound quality. I like that they can work via Bluetooth and with an analogue input because, obviously, you want to be able to use them with the plane's entertainment system. It also comes with an adapter for the split-style analogue inputs that some planes use (to keep you from stealing their headphones).

I haven't used noise cancelling headphones before this, and as I suspected, they don't work miracles, but they do help a lot. It is crazy how voices seem further away, although it will only help so much if you end up between a yappy couple that didn't want to sit directly beside each other for some reason. It does block out a lot of other sounds completely. It is just white noise (if it's more than that, I wouldn't know what), so the effects vary depending on what you are trying to cancel.

Interesting that the music you are listening to sound different depending if you have noise cancelling on or not. They both sound good, but I think it sounds better with noise cancelling on, oddly enough. I listen to loud stuff, but I suspect some people might like to pair the noise cancelling with some kind of light music or bird noises or something to try to sleep on a plane.

Obviously, the inherent drawback is that if you're using these to try to sleep on a plane, you now have something big on your head limiting the positions in which your head can take. But they are about as comfortable as any could possibly be, I think.

Nice case comes with it. They fold up in a crazy way that surprised me slightly the first time. The one thing I identified that should have been better: there is a sort of needless wrist strap on the case that starts where the zipper starts. If they put it on the other side, where the zipper ends, then you could fold it into the case when you don't want it. Of course, you can just cut it off if you don't ever want it.

These are enough to get you dirty looks from the flight attendants for not hearing them when they speak directly to you. Use with some common sense.
text_fidelity_b: Active Noise Cancelling Headphone Built-in Mic Over Ear Wireless Bluetooth Headphone Foldable Hi-Fi Stereo Headset with Wired Mode for Airplanes Travel TV PC Cell Phones

Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case These headphones are advertised more for business use than for music. The business features do work great. There is a bluetooth adapter included in the package so you can use the headphones with PCs that don't have built-in bluetooth. You can connect the headphones to 2 different bluetooth sources simultaneously so you can have a Skype call on your laptop and connect to your smartphone at the same time. There is a nice pass-through mode that lets you listen to your surroundings (or not) by pushing a button on the Jabra app.

Speaking of the app, the included manual is very skimpy and really unnecessary. To use these headphones you should download the Jabra app to your phone or PC and use the app to pair and configure the headphones. Many of the features are only available through the app.

Sound quality of the headphone is great for business use, very solid with no connection problems. For music, this is not the best I have heard from "true wireless" headphones. Some music-focused "true wireless" headphones that I own have better clarity and detail. The Jabra app does have an equalizer feature, but the effect is more subtle than what I get from other headphones.

These headphones are very comfortable and very secure, actually surprisingly secure for headphones that don't have any wings or clips. 3 different size ear tips are included, though no memory foam tips like you get with some headphones in this price range.

Battery life is 5 hours per charge and you can recharge twice with the included carrying case. That's good for "true wireless" headphones.

I would give these headphones 5 stars if the sound quality was better. It does have good business features and those are the main focus of this product. Bluetooth connection is very solid and build quality is great. 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation) UPDATE 1/5/14: I'm downgrading my rating of this keyboard to three stars for one main reason: there are very sharp edges on the inside of the two sides of this split keyboard which can cut your wrists if you aren't careful. I put my mouse in between the two sides of the keyboard because that is the best position for it for me to prevent back and arm strain. Unfortunately, every time I use the mouse, my right wrist runs into the sharp edges of the inside of the right side of this split keyboard. To give you an idea how bad this sharpness is, I wear a [[ASIN:B008C27UPQ sport wristband]] to protect my wrist, and it is literally shredding from coming in contact with the knife-sharp plastic edge. I have tried putting duct tape over the sharp edge, but it won't stick to the plastic this keyboard is made of, and to add insult to injury, the tape looks awful.

Previous Review:

I recently had a bad flare-up of right arm pain from repetitive stress. I experimented to figure out which movements at my computer were hurting me the most, and I realized that reaching for the mouse was even more painful than keyboarding. As a result, I searched for keyboards here on Amazon with the potential to be divided in half, so that I could place my mouse right in front of me. That search led me to this keyboard.

This "freestyle" keyboard gives you the option to either leave the two sides hooked together and place it at a 45-degree angle on each side, or unhook the two sides totally. It is a simple procedure, no tools required, to unhook the two sides.

This product comes with instructions for putting the keyboard together from scratch, but everything came assembled except for mounting the padding that supposedly goes under your wrists--I have medium-sized hands, and the padding lands at the base of my hands, nowhere near my wrists. The padding also is not very thick, and I'm not sure why the manufacturer did not just go ahead and paste on the padding themselves--it's a hassle making sure it is totally straight before you stick it on. It can't be re-positioned if you mess up. Fortunately, I didn't mess up, and I don't have a huge need to support my wrists, so I am not downgrading my rating for that, but some consumers might want to know about it.

I really like the ability to put my mouse pad in between the two halves. This works as well as I had hoped to prevent the strain of reaching for the mouse constantly. The keys have a nice feel to them, as well. I am a touch typist, and I was very concerned at first that I would lose that ability on a strange keyboard. I have learned after multiple long days of using the keyboard that the trick is to get my fingers in the right position to begin with, such that my right pointer finger is on the J, and my left pointer finger is on the F. Even so, I currently hit false keys much more than normal. I hope that time and use will overcome this issue. I have ordered an additional one of these keyboards to hook up to my laptop so that I am always employing the same keyboarding reflexes, in order to more quickly retrain my brain.

This keyboard is certainly much more expensive than the $15-19 keyboards I've used forever, but will be well worth the price if it, as I think it will, helps prevent the excruciating pain of repetitive stress syndrome.

This keyboard is made so that the inner section can be elevated at either of two selected heights, or it can be fairly flat. This is useful for varying the position of the hands. As a physical therapist told me years ago, changing position and resting are crucial for preventing repetitive stress. I've tried all three levels, and I find the highest one the most comfortable.

Another plus of this keyboard is that I can now bilaterally employ a beneficial PT suggestion: I have for years placed a pillow under my right arm which is positioned against the arm of my [[ASIN:B000PWGZOI rolling office chair]]. This takes the strain off my arm and shoulder by bracing them. The fact that I'm using a pillow means that I am not in danger of damaging the brachial plexus nerve in the axilla (underarm), which can happen with hard objects like crutches. Previously, it never felt comfortable when I used a traditional keyboard to do this for my left arm, but with this keyboard, it does. Now, with both arms/shoulders braced, I find that it is much easier and even automatic to keep my back straight and my head up. It has greatly eased not just arm and hand strain, but back, shoulders and neck strain as well. In addition, I make a point to take my hands completely off the keyboard and mouse when reading, vs. keyboarding, and the pillows give me a comfortable place to elevate my hands, on the top of the pillow where it extends from beneath my underarm.

I rate this product as follows:
Ease of use: 4 stars (should improve with practice)
Functionality for preventing muscle strain: 5 stars
Comfort of use on wrist: 3 stars
Ease of assembly: 4 stars
Attractiveness of keyboard: 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation)

It is portable enough to lug over to your buddy's house for play dates, but it is too bulky and heavy to carry to work everyday. Construction is very good with an aggressive-looking aluminum case to match the aggressive-sounding "Legion" product name. Mechanical keyboard has decent (but not the best) travel and the large keys are backlit so you can easily play your games in the dark. Dolby Atmos audio works well for games, but is kind of thin for music or movies unless you hook it up to external speakers. This Y720 version has a 1080p IPS display, which is OK but not as bright or contrasty as some other laptops I have used. There is also a more expensive 4K display available, but I have not tried that.

Core i7 CPU with 16GB of RAm gives you really great performance. This machine is easily powerful enough for any games I tried on it. Even though performance is throttled somewhat when run off the battery, battery life is still less than 2 hours under heavy use (maybe 6 hours with light use).

For the money, it is hard to go wrong with these Lenovo Legions. If you don't want to spend more than $1000, the cheaper Legion Y520 is almost as good for most types of games and costs $300 less.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** I'm typing this review on this Chromebook right now! I'm a graduate student, and I got tired of my Windows computer installing updates every time I opened my laptop. It was frustrating. I just wanted to open my laptop and get right to writing my homework. Now I can! It's also very lightweight, so I can easily bring it and all my books with me to class. It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

iPad Stand TechMatte Multi-Angle Aluminum Holder for Tablets, E-Readers and Smartphones, Nintendo Switch - Mini Stand The heft of this stand is impressive. I was expecting a lightweight stand, but was really surprised at how heavy and solid it was when I took it out of the box. It's the type of stand that I get the impression that I could run over with my car and not damage it. The hinge and the "kick stand" portion are made of plastic, but they also feel substantial.

The angle is set by depressing a button in the hinge area. It's very easy to adjust, and the hinge has click stops at various angles that hold it securely.

What is not adjustable is the depth of the cutout that holds the tablet or phone. I didn't have any problems with it holding a variety of tablets (iPad, Kindle and Nexus). It won't, however, hold some tablets that have a skin on it. The cutout that holds the table is slanted, and is 10mm at the widest point at the top, and 8mm at the narrowest point at the bottom. You'll want to measure your tablet plus skin to make sure it fits.

The cutout for the tablet has a plastic non-skid insert that works well. The stand itself also has plastic nubs on the back to prevent scratches on the tablet, and nubs on the bottom to prevent scratches on the table top. The nubs also act as non-skid points.

Very solid build quality, very easy to adjust in a variety of angles, and the design ensures that there won't be any damage to the tablet when you take if off/put it on the stand. As long as the width does not present a problem, this is a great choice for a tablet stand. Highly recommend.

Razer Kraken BT Kitty Edition: Bluetooth 5.0-40ms Low Latency Connection - Custom-Tuned 40mm Drivers - Beamforming Microphone - Powered Chroma - Quartz Pink The Razer Kraken BT Kitty headset is not a serious gaming headset. The lighting effects and cat ears look cool, and it’s Bluetooth so no wires like the original Kraken Kitty -- those are the big pros.

Razer Synapse does not recognize the headset, so if you want to customize it, two different phone apps are needed.

The Razer Chroma RGB app handles lighting options. The Razer Audio app handles sound settings, firmware updates, and changing the auto shutoff timer.

Do I really want to use my phone to manage my gaming headset? No. I consider having to use my phone while I’m playing a game on my computer to be a hassle!

I did find that I could customize the lighting effects with my phone, unpair the headphones from my phone and then pair them with my computer to keep the lighting effects while using with my computer. But that is also a hassle, considering Razer has a program meant to handle this!

Sound quality is just okay -- it’s not great. I’m not an audiophile so it works for me, but I have less expensive headphones that have better playback, even to my inexperienced ears. The headphones do not have ANC and I miss that a lot.

The controls are basic, a volume wheel and a power button. The power button can be used to pause and play, just hold it in for two seconds and let go, and the music will pause. Hold in for two seconds and let go to resume.

The headphones don’t have a 3.5mm audio jack, they are only Bluetooth. The charging cable is micro USB.

I have the Kraken Kitty wired headset, and I wanted a wireless version because once I started using Bluetooth headphones, I couldn’t stand being chained at my desk by a wire. But I feel like Razer wanted to appeal to women gamers -- make it pink, slap on kitty ears -- and didn’t focus as much on quality or function.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Kraken BT Kitty Edition: Bluetooth 5.0-40ms Low Latency Connection - Custom-Tuned 40mm Drivers - Beamforming Microphone - Powered Chroma - Quartz Pink

Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules There has been an unpleasant shift, from who is responsible for supplying the power adapters for USB powered appliances. And, for the number of simple household appliances that now require those adapters. I suppose that I can see the logic in it. Newer electrical devices now require lower power. Thence, adapters. At first, they came with the device, like cell phones were supplied with the wall adapters. Eventually, you had to buy your own adapters. Even now, you have to be careful in selecting an adapter. There are basic ones that only have 3 amps. Some have 5 amps or more. Some only split all their power between multiple ports. Some are 'smart' and provide all the amps needed to multiple devices. Now, that's pretty much the rule. You gotta do it yourself and you better know what you're looking for. Disappointment is more common than satisfaction, in this new game.

These outlet adapters from Mifusa probably wouldn't have been my optimum choice, had the listing been a little more informative. But, based on what I read and how it works, it will do well enough.

The six outlets are too close together for bulky plugs or those that have the transformers built into the plugs. The total amperage across all three USB ports is only 3 amps. So, don't look to power multiple USB devices efficiently. BUT, you CAN plug six AC (that's alternating current, not air conditioning) of a low enough power draw, and three USB powered devices, IF they will all fit in the MIFUSA device, and know that they also have surge protection, as indicated by the little green light.

One star being crap and five stars being spectacular, I rate these as being 'okay'.
text_fidelity_b: Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules

There are obviously a few downsides when it comes to VA monitors, but this particular model solves most of them.

I have 2 IPS displays on both sides of this, and I can tell you the colors look excellent. It was also close to perfect calibration right out of the box, which was a nice change.

One review mentioned Gamma Mode 1 as closer to 2.2, but another comment mentioned Gamma Mode 3. Mode 3 seemed closest to me when calibrating, so I would recommend it.

Viewing angles:

The viewing angles aren't very good, as expected, but it doesn't affect me as I'm always right in front of my monitors. There is some slight vignetting when sitting close, so a curved screen could have been nice if implemented well.

Backlight bleed:

Having no IPS glow or backlight bleed is another benefit. With larger VA tvs there can occasionally be some slight blobbiness when in very dark settings, but this panel is very uniform with no BLB that I can see.

Size/pixel density:

I personally love bigger monitors, and don't have an issue with the pixel density here. Some people who are more sensitive to that might not be completely satisfied, but I personally would choose the increased immersion of a larger panel. Regardless, 1440p is awesome.

Ghosting/input lag:

In terms of ghosting, it's surprisingly almost nonexistent. Here's some comments from other people:

"I played some Doom last night, and literally did nothing but rapidly move my camera all over the place to see if I could notice any ghosting or bleeding. I couldn't find anything objectionable..."

"Also there is very little ghosting in the monitor which is super rare for VA panels."

"...even in dark games like Outlast 2/Doom, the ghosting is so hard to see that you have to intentionally find a worst case scenario to try and induce it."

"Ghosting is slight, about on par with 165 Hz IPS gaming panels from my testing. Only TN is faster really."

In terms of input lag, tftcentral says: "We measured a total display lag of only 6.40ms. With approximately 4.15ms of that accounted for by pixel response times we had an estimated signal processing of just 2.25ms, which was next to nothing. This is in keeping with other G-sync screens we have tested, as the absence of an additional scaler (and presence of the G-sync module) allows for extremely low lag."

This monitor is exactly what I've been waiting for. The circular light bar on the back is a nice touch as well, although it could be a bit brighter. I also would have preferred a sharpness slider, but it's not entirely necessary.

FYI, it can be freely moved in basically every direction, including 90 degree rotation - if you need that for some reason.

So if you don't have issues with viewing angles/slightly higher pixel density, this is an excellent choice as it excels in basically every other area.
text_fidelity_b: LG 32GK850G-B 32" QHD Gaming Monitor with 144Hz Refresh Rate and NVIDIA G-Sync,Black

VideoSecu 2 Heavy Duty PA DJ Club Adjustable Height Satellite Speaker Stand Mount - Extends 26.5" to 47" (i.e. Bose, Harmon Kardon, JBL, KEF, Klipsch, Sony, Yamaha, Pioneer and Others) 1B7 These are very flimsy stands. They may be ok with small speakers (e.g. small bookshelf speakers or monitors with 4" woofers) when set to the shortest possible height, but I wouldn't even think of putting a PA speaker on one of these. The dimensions of the base is 8" x 8". Unless you are planning to bolt them to the ground, you definitely don't want to put a speaker cabinet that is heavier than 10lbs or wider than 6" on one of these. Because of the single (and small diameter) pole design, stability is very poor, no matter what how much you tighten the screws or center-balance your speakers. The side arms that are supposed to cradle the bottoms of the speakers from the sides is a mechanically poor design. The platform that the speaker sits on is only 4" deep. Given that a lot of monitor speakers are deep and the weight is distributed in the front (woofer) and back (plate amplifier), front-back wobble will be nearly impossible to eliminate.

The only way to use these speaker stands in a safe way for 5.25" or 6.25" bookshelf speakers would be to bolt the bottom plates on a sturdy piece of wood or MDF that is at least 12"x12".
text_fidelity_b: VideoSecu 2 Heavy Duty PA DJ Club Adjustable Height Satellite Speaker Stand Mount - Extends 26.5" to 47" (i.e. Bose, Harmon Kardon, JBL, KEF, Klipsch, Sony, Yamaha, Pioneer and Others) 1B7

Apple MFi Certified Lightning Cable 3 Pack 10 FT，Nylon Braided iPhone Charger Fast Charging iPhone Charger Cord Super Long Compatible with iPhone 13 12 11 Pro Max XR XS X 8 7 6 Plus SE iPad and More I learned the (almost) hard way, it’s a really bad idea to go cheap on cables. I had a few of the discount store kind. I was out of the house, and one was so distressed from normal use, moving it around to put the device where I needed it or use it while charging, that the wiring caught fire. Burned through the cable. Burned through the plastic box of (thankfully not the alcohol-based Pro) Tombow brush pens, burned into a pen, hit the dyed water, and was extinguished. I was so freaked, I checked every one of those cheap wires, and sure enough, there was a scary amount of damage just from routine wear. The price of cheap cables is way too high.

I threw all my old lighting cables out and upgraded to these, and I’m glad I did. These are sturdy. I’ve twisted them. I’ve put stress on them. I don’t need a repeat performance of house fire cable. I want to know I can rely on these, and so far, I’m not seeing any cause for concern. The outer sheaf is thick enough and tough enough to protect the wiring within, and the connection to the port ends are sturdy and quite secure. They go all the way into the port cover, not end at the tip.

If these give me any trouble, I will come back here and update the review, but after that incident made me gun shy, I’ve checked these as thoroughly as I can and they look sturdy to me. They have ample length and the work just fine.
text_fidelity_b: Apple MFi Certified Lightning Cable 3 Pack 10 FT，Nylon Braided iPhone Charger Fast Charging iPhone Charger Cord Super Long Compatible with iPhone 13 12 11 Pro Max XR XS X 8 7 6 Plus SE iPad and More

Denon D-M41 Home Theater Mini Amplifier and Bookshelf Speaker Pair - Compact HiFi Stereo System with CD, FM/AM Tuner and Wireless Bluetooth Music | Perfect for Small Rooms and Home Cinema It was time to upgrade my home stereo. I've had it for decades, and I also needed a CD player. After a bunch of research, I settled on this as a solution. Moving from a full-sized receiver and larger speakers to this was actually fairly refreshing. Here are some thoughts:

Build quality
Everything felt solid when taking it out of the box. The speakers also had a nice heft. The remote felt great, too. Once I got it set up, all the buttons had a nice feel, the volume knob was smooth, and the CD tray opened/closed in a very smooth fashion. Taking a look at the back, you have all the connections you'll need for most purposes.

Sound
I was VERY impressed at how clear this thing is. It's my first "HiFi" system, and a huge improvement over the old Aiwa/Bose system that I had. When I was gearing up to buy this, I figured I might need a small subwoofer to provide a bit of low frequency support. That's not the case at all for music! These little speakers pump out rich and full sound. I may still invest in a small sub for movies, however.

CD/Bluetooth
My primary uses for this will be for music. The CD player handles all my CDs just fine (including the "enhanced" CDs that my previous players failed to play.) Connecting this to my phone was a snap, and the Bluetooth audio sounded just fine (for Bluetooth.)

Overall, this is a little powerhouse of a system, and I can't be happier.
text_fidelity_b: Denon D-M41 Home Theater Mini Amplifier and Bookshelf Speaker Pair - Compact HiFi Stereo System with CD, FM/AM Tuner and Wireless Bluetooth Music | Perfect for Small Rooms and Home Cinema

text_fidelity_a: Arlo VMC4030-100NAR PRO Add-on Camera, White (Renewed) I received my Arlo Pro ahead of the delivery schedule. It was packaged nicely/professionally even though it is refurbished & came with charging/mounting accessories. I already have 3 Arlo cameras from before and wanted to add an additional camera and read that the Arlo Pro worked more efficiently than the Arlo 2. I struggled the first night setting it up (otherwise a very fast system to set up). I had placed it in a window which prohibited the motion device, so I ended up mounting it outside (and I do purchase the silicon skins to protect my devices) with the suggestion of Tech support and it works beautifully now (tech support wait time was less than 2 minutes on a Sunday afternoon/PST). At first, the camera appeared to have a glitch with a constant flashing, so I removed the battery and reinserted it and it was fine. Tech support was able to remote into my cameras to test whether it was getting Wifi, optimized settings, signals, etc. which was very helpful in figuring out where I was having my issue. Video is in color; it records sounds excellently; AND has a mic which I haven't accessed yet. All added features can be customized or turned off altogether (i.e., sound). In trying to set up my Pro, I watched a few Arlo videos which introduced me to the "MODE" tab option which then allowed me to access ALL my cameras in customizing my cameras better than just going straight into DEVICE tab. Not confirmed, but I think the MODE overrides any settings that you would do to your device if you go directly into DEVICE tab. Select MODE tab, then select your BASE, then click on your cameras individually & SAVE. Having accessed the MODE, ALL my cameras are now working much better. I get email alerts (which is set under MODE & can be turned off if you wish). I have had my Arlo system since 2016 and with my new addition, can't beat the price and reliability of the device. However, I do clean the lenses periodically for optimum motion detection. I do like that the Arlo Pro is rechargeable because my other 3 are not and it costs me about $40 in batteries every 3 months (those cameras take 4 batteries each).  If you find video you want to save, you can download it to your PC/Smart Phone for safe keeping; otherwise, Arlo Cloud clears your video library on the 7th day (which comes with the camera free with the option to subscribe to Arlo if you want a longer history). Bottom-line, you can purchase this system and grow it to meet your needs and upgrade cameras to which the base will support it. I can access https://arlo.netgear.com/#/login via PC or SmartPhone to view my LIBRARY. I do recommend updating your phone app periodically.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo VMC4030-100NAR PRO Add-on Camera, White (Renewed)

text_fidelity_a:
RHA MA750 (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I dislike reviews where the comments just gush about the product. But I have no other choice but to do just that - these are some incredibly good earphones!

I've been using RHA earphones for a couple of years and have been impressed by the sound quality given the price. I own several earphones, but the ones I reach for most often by far are my RHA MA350s even though they are one of the least pricey pair of buds I own. Great sound quality and excellent build quality.

Well, the MA350s will be spending some time on the shelf. The MA750s are a clear step up. (Gush alert:) These are simply amazing! They can handle anything I thrown at them so far, with great bass that doesn't boom or bottom out, clear midrange and sharp upper range. Just fantastic performance.

I was a bit concerned about the ear wrap design since I usually find that type of design to be irritating for long-term use, and especially irritating when wearing them while exercising. But no problems at all even with extended wearing. Very comfortable and no chafing even when running.

The MA750s come with an extensive set of replacement ear cushions in a variety of designs. I can't imagine that a person would not be able to adjust these to fit perfectly given there are 10 different potential configurations. The cord is stout but flexible, with significant reenforcements at the plug end.

Even the packaging is upscale, with a high quality box with a front panel (with a magnetic enclosure) that opens to revel the earphones and tips nicely displayed. Very Apple-esque in their presentation.

Also included is a leather (or what feels like leather) carry case. The tips come with a metal holder that fits into the case so you can keep everything neatly stored and protected. A small point, but is shows that some real thought went into every aspect of this product.

While these are priced higher than other RHA earphones, the cost is well worth it. Even at the current price point, these outperform my Bose, Shure and Sennheiser earbuds that are priced far higher, and way outperform buds in their MA750 price range.

Huge recommendation for these - try as I might, I just can't find a single criticism to voice about them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: RHA MA750 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I have been using the Kindle for exactly one week and it has exceeded my expectations in every way except for one design flaw.

Downloading books is absolutely a breeze and the selection of titles (for a premier launch of a product) is simply outstanding. I cannot wait to see what else will be added in the future and my credit card is ready and waiting.

Figuring out how to use the Kindle was easier than figuring out my basic LG cellphone. I am, obviously, a technical loser, but the Kindle has made me feel like a genius. This the best Christmas gift I could have hoped for. I am now in the process of reading 6 different books, with 2 more in the queue. Not to mention 3 blogs which I check throughout the day.

The Kindle has opened up new worlds for me and is giving me the opportunity to discover subjects that I would never have considered in a million years. And why not? Instead of stacking books throughout my house, I can now carry them around in a compact unit which is lighter than a paperback.

I don't know who to thank for this wonderful creation, but I can assure you that I will be a customer for life.

text_fidelity_a:
Magellan RoadMate 1470 4.7-Inch Widescreen Portable GPS Navigator I've been a Magellan user for several years - have owned four of their GPS systems, and always appreciate how they have improved their products. This unit is my 5th, and replaces a Magellan 4040. After using it for a while I've confident in saying this is the best one yet!

The most visible change is the actual size of the unit. The screen size has been increased, but the unit is thinner and lighter. Very sleek appearance, and the screen is a real joy -- sharp, clear graphics even in the sun, and bigger on-screen buttons for easy use. The mounting system has also been streamlined, and looks and works well. It mounts very easily on a NavMat holder (basically a bean-bag system that I got on Amazon. I'm a huge Navmat fan - makes it a snap to hide the GPS with narry a trace. Best accessory by far for any GPS).

The power connector was not well thought out, however. You have to connect it to the GPS unit AFTER you mount it in the holder. They should have moved the connector it a wee bit to the side to avoid that.

The only button is a slide-type power button on the top. Boot-up time is OK -- not speedy, but not a huge delay either. It does not have a "sleep" mode, so you have to do a cold boot every time. Not a problem in real world use - by the time you get situated in your car, the unit is ready to go.

Voice is clear and easy to understand. Not as natural sounding as a TomTom, but understandable.

Pretty much any recent GPS unit will get you where you want to go. I've found the routing on the Magellans to be very similar to Garmins - could be because they both use the same mapping set (Navteq). The Magellan shines, however, in features that I find helpful. The direction of the next turn is always visible regardless of how far away the next turn will be. Up until recently, Garmin did not offer this (they do now on some of their units). Sounds like a small issue, but I find it very helpful. The Magellan also allows you to very easily exclude a route (or portion). That's a fairly standard feature nowadays, but Magellan allows you to do it in a snap.

In terms of routing, Magellan offers four options (fastest, shortest, most use of freeways and least use). You can see all four options on the map (as a summary) at the same time so you can pick the best one for your needs. Perfect!!

Love the AAA Guidebook, which is a unique Magellan feature. Lets you get details about restaurants and other points of interest just like the paper version from AAA. I used it a lot in my 4040, especially when traveling out of town.

Other unique Magellan features I appreciate is the "ding dong" sound right before a turn (incredibly accurate!) and the fact that the software reminds you to "stay on the current road" when you encounter major exits. Some find that to be nagging, but it has saved me from inadvertently exiting on more than one occasion.

A new feature for Magellan is the lane guidance. Very nicely done. I've used this feature on Navigon units, and found it rather unhelpful. Magellan's implementation is far more useful, with better, clearer graphics. However, lane guidance is not available for every road.

The software is also nicely done - very logical to use. If you're a past Magellan user you can pick this up and use it in a second. If not, there's a short printed user's guide in the box (plus a CD-ROM with more in-depth info) that gets you up to speed quickly. The box also includes the mount, power connector for the car, and a USB cable. It does not include an AC adapter.

OK, now for the bad news. When it comes to customer service, Magellan has been horrid. We're talking so bad it's almost funny. I'm hoping this situation will change - the company was bought by Mitac late last year, and perhaps this will signal a change for the better in terms of customer support. Lord knows, they couldn't get any worse.

The leader, in my opinion, for customer support is Garmin. They are nice to deal with on the phone, answer emails promptly, and offer regular firmware updates. Whenever I buy a GPS as a gift I always buy Garmin since I don't want to saddle the recipient with the miserable service that Magellan offers. It's a shame, since Magellan offers some real benefits over Garmin, and more value for the money. Tom Tom is also decent when it comes to support, but they use TeleAtlas maps which are less complete than NavTeq (sp?).

Bottom line -- if you're looking for a straightforward GPS at a good price, this should be on your short list. It lacks features such as Bluetooth and an MP3 player, but for me, I want a GPS to offer guidance and not entertainment. This has a very robust feature set, great screen, and well-designed software. It also has traffic capabilities -- did not test that feature out, so I can't comment on it.

The "safe" bet continues to be Garmin. You'll pay a bit more, and get less features, but you can be assured of solid support. Whether Magellan's new owners will put them back on the right track (if you'll excuse the horrid, but unavoidable pun) in terms of customer service is not yet clear. I hope so -- they make a great product!

UPDATE: 5/21/09 There's a firmware update on the Magellan site. No new functionality (in terms of new features) but, according to the release notes it improves overall performance. Easy to install - just follow the included step-by-step instructions. It seems like it makes the unit a bit faster, but that could just be my imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Magellan RoadMate 1470 4.7-Inch Widescreen Portable GPS Navigator

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Tablet Mouse for Android 3.1+ You just cannot go wrong with a Logitech mouse, and this one is no exception. Sleek and sexy, well-designed and reliable, this tablet mouse for Android 3.1+ is a joy to hold. I love the color, too. It reminds me of my beloved old teal Logitech corded mouse that wouldn't work with the newer computers. This is a notebook-sized mouse, which is the size I prefer. It is not as tiny as some of the little mice out there, though. Not too big, not to small; just right.

Logitech stresses that this is an Android mouse and that it's not going to work properly with anything older than Android 3.1. It's even in the product title, so it's obvious that the OS is important, but I'm sure there will be people out there who will think it's going to work with earlier versions of Android. I wouldn't chance it. Some other reviewers have reported successfully pairing this mouse with non-Android systems, but I haven't been able to. It did happily meet and greet a friend's tablet PC, however.

Note that, unlike some Logitech mice, this mouse does NOT have a dongle, so you must have a bluetooth-enabled machine to use it. I tried it with a generic bluetooth dongle on my Windows Vista laptop, and I couldn't get it to work. That's not the mouse's fault. One good thing about it is that you can use it with a bluetooth keyboard; if I were going to get one, I'd go with Logitech's keyboard so I know they'll play nice.

I haven't had the opportunity to run down the batteries of this mouse, but if this one is like the other Logitech mice I own, the batteries last a long, long time--unlike competitors' mice, which seem to chew up and spit out batteries every few weeks. You can turn the mouse off, of course, but the sleep function also conserves batteries. Very nice.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Tablet Mouse for Android 3.1+

text_fidelity_a:
Polk Audio Atrium 6 Outdoor Speakers with Bass Reflex Enclosure (Pair, Black) - All-Weather Durability | Broad Sound Coverage | Speed-Lock Mounting System The Good:
-They sound good. They're not audiophile speakers, of course, but they sound much better than some of the other outdoor speakers I've heard, and better than any other outdoor speaker I auditioned in this price range.
-They're rugged, which you really need in an outdoor speaker. It's not just rain, after all; an outdoor speaker has to contend with errant footballs, rough handling, curious animals, etc, any of which would break a normal indoor speaker. These have a metal grill and very sturdy build and should stand up to almost anything.
-I like the mounting system; very flexible and well-engineered.

The Bad (and these are minor)
-Very cramped, awkward space for the binding posts. I use banana plugs because I need a quick, easy way to hook them up (standing on a ladder, fumbling around behind the speaker) and there's not enough room back there for normal banana plugs. I wound up buying some right-angle plugs (I got the Monoprice), and those resolved this for me.
-Sound quality is good for an outdoor speaker in this price range but if you don't need a rugged speaker, you can get much better sound for the price. As I'm writing this review, the ELAC Debut 2.0 B6.2 is on sale for about the same price as these Atriums, and the ELAC has much better sound. Of course, the ELAC probably wouldn't survive a night on my patio.

Bottom line: If you need an outdoor speaker in this price range, this speaker would be my recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Polk Audio Atrium 6 Outdoor Speakers with Bass Reflex Enclosure (Pair, Black) - All-Weather Durability | Broad Sound Coverage | Speed-Lock Mounting System

Pairing was super simple. I turned the headset on and then turned the bluetooth on. Within seconds I was paired. No special codes, no jumping through hoops. It worked, right out of the box. BTW, I have a Sony Experia Android phone.

I don't know where they get the 300 foot distance thing. The most I got was 108 feet during my test. I used one of those rolling rulers the contractors use. text_fidelity_a:
Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black This is my first purchase of earbuds in the over $200 category. I got the Jabra Elite 65t as soon as they came out and have since bought a couple of other pairs of earbuds in the under $100 category that had better features like IPX7 or 8hr battery life. Therefore I was excited to upgrade to the XM4 for their bettery life and the noise canceling.

Unfortunately, I've had several issues with these. I don't have particularly small ears. Usually the medium tips fit without issue. On the XM4, I started with the medium tips and tested their air tightness using the app. The small tips don't have any kind of seal on my ears without really shoving them super far down my ear canal, so I decided to stick with the medium size. Unfortunately, I have experienced significant ear fatigue enough so that I can't wear the earbuds for more than a couple of hours. I have since switched to the small tips for the sake of comfort, but that means sacrificing any passive noise canceling - and unless I have a defective unit, without the passive noise canceling in addition to the active noise canceling, there is absolutely no difference between having the noise canceling on and off. To me, this completely defeats the purpose of buying noise canceling earbuds.

I also have had issues with connectivity such as the bluetooth connection on my phone suddenly dropping and having to go into the app to manually pair them again.

In terms of battery life, depending on the control settings of each earbud, there can be a difference in the drain of battery between the left and right side. On a bad day, I had a 30% difference with the right draining significantly faster. My earbuds are using the factory settings with the playback controls on the right and the noise canceling on the left for reference.

Both the connectivity problems and the bettery difference between the earbuds has seemed to have gotten better since performing a factory reset, but be aware that there is still a little difference in the rate of battery drain between the L and R earbuds (It's not super significant now and maybe reaches under 7-8% difference at the end of the day).

I bought some Comply foam tips, which I hope will fix the discomfort issue and make the noise canceling work at the optimal rate without the ear fatigue. However, I shouldn't have to modify almost $300 earbuds to make them work like they should. It would help if Sony would offer more sizes of ear tips to help make them more usable for a wider population. Then again, if I have gripes like these, then maybe the XM4s aren't for me. Makes me super sad considering I think that they're probably fantastic for most people.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black

Point is - sound matters to me.

The overall tone is cool, not bright. That means the midrange sounds accurate and non-harsh, but not terribly warm. That's okay, I'll take cool over harsh any day.

When you first purchase them, I'd suggest letting them play for a few hours (or overnight) plugged into a sound source, so they break in a bit. I did notice an improvement afterward.

Seriously, for $100, these are great!

text_fidelity_a:
Actiontec 300 Mbps Wireless-N ADSL Modem Router (GT784WN) DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. I am a Centurylink/Qwest customer of over 25 years. I have a old Actiontec Q1000 router/modem. My DSL Ethernet connection to my desk top has gone down for hours at a time lately. My wifi goes out 10-12 times daily as of late. Small one story house with only two old, non gamer people with latest model $800 smart phones. I read the online instructions and even watched Actiontec video for installing this product. I had a problem and called 1-888-436-0657 the tech support number listed in the Quick Start Guide. Actiontec's phone answering tree makes it very clear that they will not provide any tech support for products purchased from Amazon or any other "unauthorized dealers". I pressed 0 and they hung up on me three seperate times. The Amazon listing for this product made it very clear that it would work with Centturylink. It has a big check mark for Centurylink.

I have spent so many hours on the phone, through email and chat mode with Centurylink it is embarrassing. I offered to pay Centurylink to have a tech come to my home and install my new router/modem. Centurylink said their techs were not allowed to install router/modems but would check my outside wiring for free and my inside wiring for $85 minimun. Centurylink told me they would be happy to have a tech walk me through my hookup via telephone. After I finally was connected to a Centurylink tech and was verified they advised me they were not "allowed" to offer tech support to their customers on this product. They made it sound like it was a federal felony to offer tech support on this product.

Best Buy in New Mexico, and apparently all other retailers no longer carry any products compatible with Centurylink DSL because of their refusal to offer tech support. I heard that Amazon is having so many issues with router/modems that they are reluctant to take returns. I guess I will be taking the $67 loss. I should have rememberd my latin "caveat emptor".

So now I am going to angrily switch to the second most hated consumer corporation, Xfinity. Did you know that Xfinity is Comcast with a new name? Comcast's reputation is so trashed they decided if they adopted a new name they could fool a lot of consumers. As we all know, there is no real free market with open competition. In most markets you have DSL with the only telephone company available or cable with the only cable company in your neighborhood. A pig with lipstick is still, after all just a pig. I am advising myself and everyone else to do serious due diligence before purchasing any internet electronics from any vendors. Or you could just rent the overpriced and low quality products peddled by the ISPs.
text_fidelity_b: Actiontec 300 Mbps Wireless-N ADSL Modem Router (GT784WN)

text_fidelity_a:
HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2 ...if you don't have a wrist rest or pad already, I highly recommend that you get one at the same time you get this keyboard. I was introduced to the chiclet- or scissor-style keyboard because of using one at work (using an Apple wired keyboard with an Intel Mac), and I have to say that I prefer it in every way to the more traditional keyboards. It is much quieter, and, for me, the feedback is pleasant. One thing I did not take into account, though, is that I had a wrist rest at work. So when I got this keyboard for home use and started using it, I loved it immediately--until the day I used it for hours on end. Then--ouch! My wrists began to ache.

Overall, this is a great keyboard. It connected to my computer without a problem, and the only lag in keystrokes I have experienced has been when the computer had just been "awakened" from sleep mode. For reasons I will not go into here, I am using this keyboard with a laptop: the laptop keyboard's lights indicate whether or not I have Caps Lock or Num Lock engaged on the wireless keyboard. I understand that won't help people using this keyboard with a desktop computer, but thought I'd put it out there anyway.

My conclusion: if you're a fan of the scissor-style keyboard and you have or are willing to invest in a wrist rest, you will enjoy this keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Pro Long story short I lost my airpod pros. Saw these on major discount ($90 for Black Friday), and couldn't resist. So here's my take in four parts. Sound Quality. Noise Cancelling. Ambient pass through. Features.

Sound quality -- versus the airpod pros, these are almost identical in sound. The only difference is the beats buds are a touch bass heavy. It's good, punchy bass, but noticeably more than the pros which were more balanced with its lows. So if you're a bass head, or hip-hop enthusiast, the beats win hands down.

Noise cancelling -- now this could have to do with the shape of my ear, but I found the beats to actually be a step ABOVE in noise cancelling. My gf still has her airpods and I compared. The seal the beat creates, paired with its noise cancelling makes it seem like the world doesn't exist. Beats win for me in NC.

Ambient pass-through -- this is where the beats lose out. Their noise cancelling is too good. So even when you have transparency turned on the world sound a little muddied out, while with the airpods, if I had transparency on it was almost like I wasn't wearing them. I miss that alot. So if you are in an environment where you need to hear what people are saying without removing your buds then airpods might be your pick. It's not to say that beats mak you deaf or anything but things are just noticeably quieter in transparance vs airpods with its full clarity.

Features -- another loss for the beats. They don't work with the beats app so no equalizer function... why beats???? WHY?? So you'll have to go third party if you want to equalize. The beats also won't stop the music or video you're watching if one falls out. No biggy for me as I like that but some people might not. Other than that it has similar functionality to airpods. One click to pause, two to skip, etc. It doesn't auto switch between devices but does actually switch pretty similarly. Takes maybe two clicks to switch it to my mac. The pairing is a breeze with iphones. Just open the case next to your iphone and voila. It's paired.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Pro

I think that also contributes to the feeling that the buttons are hard to click, they really aren't, it's just you have to have a death grip on the mouse sometimes and it's perceived that you do. Perhaps something less slick or some bumps or grooves to lend a little traction would be a good option. I've actually been looking for something I can stick there to give me a slightly rougher surface. Anyway, just a thought.

The mouse is very responsive and easy to adapt to, it works like a mouse on it's side so no having to get used to a strange and new configuration. I do not have carpal tunnel so can't say that it helped me there. But I feel I got a good mouse for the money. Less slickness in the thumb area would have earned it 5 stars.

StarTech.com SATA to USB Cable - USB 3.0 to 2.5” SATA III Hard Drive Adapter - External Converter for SSD/HDD Data Transfer (USB3S2SAT3CB) I tried this cable with a Samsung EVO 850 240GB drive which I already had tested in a $16.99 Inatek UASB USB 3.0 enclosure (purchased on Amazon).

This UBS 3.1 cable is slower. If you look at the attached photos, the first is the drive with this cable and the 2nd is the exact same drive in the cheap USB 3.0 enclosure. Same computer. This is running the CrystalMark DiskMark 64S benchmarking tool, which is designed to effectively test SSDs.

Disappointing performance. On the plus side, it's certainly simpler to install (the Inatek requires 6 SMALL screws, which is kinda bonkers).
An SSD has no real need of the enclosure. So this seems like it would be a better solution. But not if speed matters.
The benchmark is automatically run 5x and I ran the whole thing twice because I expected this cable to be faster.

text_fidelity_a: TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50) Powerful dual-band router. Easy to set up, even though I managed to take a few wrong turns on the way. Get your phone and take a photo of the password on the bottom of the router after you have it connected and before you sit down to get everything functioning. I'd purchased a cheap router last year and this product tells me that buying the cheapest kind isn't always a bright idea -- this router is much more powerful and a lot faster than the El Cheapo I had. My kids ought to be thrilled, they both play online games. When I want to scare them, I tell them stories about 14.4K modems from 25 years ago... This router was easy to set up, comes with very clear instructions (so simple a guy can follow them). Now that I have it set up, the things I stumbled over seem inconsequential. I'm on a Mac, so things are fairly clear anyway, compared to Windows. This router is a major upgrade from the hardware I had been using. Now -- should I tell my kids the 5GHz password or let them use the 2.4GHz speeds?!?
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50)

SanDisk Ultra 32GB UHS-I/Class 10 Micro SDHC Memory Card With Adapter - SDSDQUAN-032G-G4A After I bought this 64 GB micro SD card, I put it in a box with my other SD and micro SD cards until I bought my new phone last year. I installed it with my new phone and SIM card.
Since that time, I have been unable to 'see' the micro SD card, so I could not set it to be used for all the photos and videos that I take with my phone. I connected my phone to my computer and transferred music with no problem since that was stored on my phone's internal memory. I could not download any photos, so I have been having to transfer the photos via my Google photos on my computer. I even removed the micro SD card and inserted it in my card readers and plugged one into a USB port. NOTHING.
So I inserted another micro SD card - this one is 128 GB. VOILA! I was able to see it in my computer as well as in my phone where I was able to access it as well as to format it – finally.

This micro SD card must have been defective from the start, a waste of $35. If I had used it immediately – although I didn't 'need' it at the time, I could have returned it. Now I will find out if the company really guarantees this for 10 years.

I called customer service and they were very friendly and very helpful in getting another TV sent out quickly as a replacement. The replacement works great. The TV's are easy to mount, they also came with giant legs that would not have fit our stand. The set up process is really easy and straightforward as well, it walks you through it. The picture is so clear and bright, the colors are brilliant. The sound is really clear, we have since hooked up our Sony sound bar to add to the experience. There are tons of apps to choose from, we are also hooking up a Roku because we're missing some and can't get them in the store. This is my first brand new TV and I don't think I could have picked a better one.

Update: it's been less than 2 years and we're back to no picture. The TV worked great up until last night and the picture suddenly went out. I contacted customer service who had me troubleshoot, which was turn it off and back on. I had already reset the thing hoping that would help. CS gave me the info for a repair company an hour away and said have a great day. I can't believe they make $1300 tvs to only last 2 years. Very disappointed.

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Earbuds,Kurdene Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging case,Touch Control in Ear Bluetooth 5.0 Waterproof Headphones CVC 8.0 Noise Cancelling Earphones with Deep Bass Sound for Sports(Pink) Pros

1. Excellent sound, with more clarity than the other Bluetooth earbuds I own. They are especially better for listening to music.

2. The earbuds and their case have a sleek, attractive design.

Cons

1. Each small ear piece operates separately. They are not attached to each other via a plastic-coated wire as is typically the case for earbuds. This means that, when I remove these earbuds from my ears, because there is no wire holding them securely around my neck, they must be carefully and consistently placed in their carrying case, and then either set in a safe, easily remembered location, or placed in my pants pocket. Neither option is desirable. It is extremely difficult to not get distracted and set down these earbuds in a random location, such that afterwards I have to waste a lot of time looking for them. And the problem with slipping them into a pocket is that there is a strong possibility I might accidentally leave them there, such that they end up in the washer and dryer and are ruined. In short, the risk of losing or destroying these earbuds is enormous!

2. Each ear piece must be turned ON/OFF separately, one after the other. This is a hassle.

3. The ON/OFF controls are extremely difficult to engage. You touch an ear piece and hold it for several seconds to turn each ear piece on or off. There is no button. The ear piece is somehow sensing the pressure of the touch of a fingertip. I frequently have great difficulty locating and pressing the exact spot required in order to turn these earbuds on or off. This is a major pain!

4. Volume is controlled the same way as the ON/OFF function, by magically managing to touch the earpiece in the exact, necessary location with the appropriate amount of fingertip pressure. It is very difficult to accomplish that, and the frustration of failing at this onerous task again and again is maddening!

For all of the above reasons, I wouldn’t recommend these earbuds to my worst enemy!
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Earbuds,Kurdene Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging case,Touch Control in Ear Bluetooth 5.0 Waterproof Headphones CVC 8.0 Noise Cancelling Earphones with Deep Bass Sound for Sports(Pink)
